##### Constructing the $2^{3-1}$ half-fraction design {#sec-pri-3342}

[**Construction of a $2^{3-1}$ half fraction design by starting with a $2^2$ full factorial design**]{#sec-pri-3342-overview}

First note that, mathematically, $2^{3-1} = 2^2$. This gives us the first step, which is to start with a regular $2^2$ full factorial design. That is, we start with the following design table.

| | $X_1$ | $X_2$ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | -1 | -1 |
| 2 | +1 | -1 |
| 3 | -1 | +1 |
| 4 | +1 | +1 |

: A Standard Order $2^2$ Full Factorial Design Table {#tbl-pri-3342-2x2}

[**Assign the third factor to the interaction column of a $2^2$ design**]{#sec-pri-3342-assign}

This design has four runs, the right number for a half-fraction of a $2^3$, but there is no column for factor $X_3$. We need to add a third column to take care of this, and we do it by adding the $X_1{\cdot}X_2$ interaction column. This column is, as you will recall from full factorial designs, constructed by multiplying the row entry for $X_1$ with that of $X_2$ to obtain the row entry for $X_1{\cdot}X_2$.

| | $X_1$ | $X_2$ | $X_1{\cdot}X_2$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | -1 | -1 | +1 |
| 2 | +1 | -1 | -1 |
| 3 | -1 | +1 | -1 |
| 4 | +1 | +1 | +1 |

: A $2^2$ Design Table Augmented with the $X_1{\cdot}X_2$ Interaction Column {#tbl-pri-3342-augmented}

[**Design table with $X_3$ set to $X_1{\cdot}X_2$**]{#sec-pri-3342-x3-set}

We may now substitute '$X_3$' in place of '$X_1{\cdot}X_2$' in this table.

| | $X_1$ | $X_2$ | $X_3$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | -1 | -1 | +1 |
| 2 | +1 | -1 | -1 |
| 3 | -1 | +1 | -1 |
| 4 | +1 | +1 | +1 |

: A $2^{3-1}$ Design Table with Column $X_3$ set to $X_1{\cdot}X_2$ {#tbl-pri-3342-x3-plus}

[**Design table with $X_3$ set to $-X_1{\cdot}X_2$**]{#sec-pri-3342-x3-negative}

Note that the rows of the table above give the dark-shaded corners of the design in @fig-pri-3341-cube. If we had set $X_3 = -X_1{\cdot}X_2$ as the rule for generating the third column of our $2^{3-1}$ design, we would have obtained:

| | $X_1$ | $X_2$ | $X_3$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | -1 | -1 | -1 |
| 2 | +1 | -1 | +1 |
| 3 | -1 | +1 | +1 |
| 4 | +1 | +1 | -1 |

: A $2^{3-1}$ Design Table with Column $X_3$ set to $-X_1{\cdot}X_2$ {#tbl-pri-3342-x3-minus}

[**Main effect estimates from fractional factorial not as good as full factorial**]{#sec-pri-3342-precision}

This design gives the light-shaded corners of the box of @fig-pri-3341-cube. Both $2^{3-1}$ designs that we have generated are equally good, and both save half the number of runs over the original $2^3$ full factorial design. If $c_1$, $c_2$, and $c_3$ are our estimates of the main effects for the factors $X_1$, $X_2$, $X_3$ (i.e., the difference in the response due to going from "low" to "high" for an effect), then the precision of the estimates $c_1$, $c_2$, and $c_3$ are not quite as good as for the full 8-run factorial because we only have four observations to construct the averages instead of eight; this is one price we have to pay for using fewer runs.

[**Example**]{#sec-pri-3342-example}

Example: For the 'Pressure (P), Table speed (T), and Down force (D)' design situation of the [previous example](#sec-pri-3341-industry-example), here's a replicated $2^{3-1}$ in randomized run order, with five centerpoint runs ('000') interspersed among the runs. This design table was constructed using the technique discussed above, with D = P*T.

**Design table for the example**

| | Pattern | P | T | D | Center Point |
|---:|:---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| 2 | +-- | +1 | -1 | -1 | 0 |
| 3 | -+- | -1 | +1 | -1 | 0 |
| 4 | 000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| 5 | +++ | +1 | +1 | +1 | 0 |
| 6 | --+ | -1 | -1 | +1 | 0 |
| 7 | 000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| 8 | +-- | +1 | -1 | -1 | 0 |
| 9 | --+ | -1 | -1 | +1 | 0 |
| 10 | 000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| 11 | +++ | +1 | +1 | +1 | 0 |
| 12 | -+- | -1 | +1 | -1 | 0 |
| 13 | 000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

: A $2^{3-1}$ Design Replicated Twice, with Five Centerpoint Runs Added {#tbl-pri-3342-replicated}
